mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of at least 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 1% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for 3 consecutive months at >1% monthly rate
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month
regime_hint: high inflation and rate hike regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above the 10-year average, combined with a decline in personal income growth (PAYEMS growth < 0.5%), signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces aggregate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 10-year avg AND PAYEMS growth < 0.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in a single month signals a sharp deterioration in labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An above-trend increase in the GDP price index (GDPC1) of at least 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a re-acceleration in economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
